title: Make
summary: A visual automation platform built around scenarios, module actions and monthly credits.

sources.title: Make Core pricing and annual billing

facts.label: Workflow
facts.value: Visual scenarios connect applications through triggers and actions that process data.

facts.label: Usage unit
facts.value: The pricing page describes module actions as credits and exposes selectable monthly credit quantities.

facts.label: Privacy / data handling
facts.value: The Celonis Privacy Notice for Make says it may gather application-related usage data such as user interactions and searches, viewed pages and files, data-source types, workflow-step counts, operation types and queries, system configuration, logfile data and timestamps. This describes individual-related data handling; it does not specify account-level treatment of workflow payloads or connected providers.

facts.label: Personal-data retention and deletion
facts.value: Make's Privacy Notice says personal data will be deleted on request or when it no longer serves its purpose where permitted by law, subject to longer retention for legal obligations or claims. Its Privacy & GDPR page says customers can request deletion of personal data once it is no longer required, including after subscription termination. Neither page gives a purge timeline or establishes workspace-specific scope for workflow payloads, logs or non-personal records.

facts.label: Scenario portability
facts.value: Make documents exporting an individual scenario as a JSON blueprint containing its modules, module settings and mapped values; it says blueprints can back up a scenario when switching Make accounts. An imported blueprint requires the user's own account connections and must be under 2 MB. Scenario history has a separate CSV export. Make warns that a simple-mode AES secret key is exposed when sharing a scenario or downloading its blueprint. These sources document scenario-level reuse, not full-organization recovery, and no migration was tested.

facts.label: Infrastructure hosting locations
facts.value: The pricing table lists AWS (EU/North America) for each plan. This does not establish customer-selectable regions or account-level data residency.

facts.label: Core execution log storage
facts.value: The plan comparison lists 30 days of execution log storage for Core. Deletion semantics and retention of other data are not specified here.

facts.label: Published log-data retention
facts.value: Make's security page says log data is stored for 30 days by default and Enterprise can extend the period. The page does not identify log categories or this workspace's settings; this statement is separate from Core's plan-listed 30-day execution-log allowance.

facts.label: Core data transfer allowance
facts.value: The plan table lists 5 GB of data transfer per 10,000 monthly credits; this is an allowance, not a measured workload estimate.

prices.name: Free
prices.billing: Free plan; official page says there is no time limit.

prices.name: Core (10,000 credits/month; annual billing)
prices.billing: Make lists USD 9/month equivalent for 10,000 monthly credits on annual billing; this is not the upfront annual total or regional checkout quote.
prices.allowance: 10,000 credits per month at the selected pricing quantity.

prices.name: Core (10,000 credits/month; monthly billing)
prices.billing: The Make pricing selector lists USD 12/month at the 10,000-credit tier with monthly payment; local taxes and checkout total depend on location.
prices.allowance: 10,000 credits per month at the selected pricing quantity.
prices.taxes: Location-dependent checkout taxes are not captured.

sections.heading: Count actions, not just scenarios
paragraphs: List each trigger and module action in a representative scenario and estimate its run frequency. Retries, polling and data transfer can change the monthly credit requirement, so validate the estimate against a bounded trial.

sections.heading: Verify the billing selector
paragraphs: For 10,000 monthly credits, Make lists USD 12/month with monthly payment or USD 9/month equivalent on annual billing. Confirm location-dependent taxes, checkout details and extra-credit rules before budgeting.

sections.heading: Rehearse scenario recovery
paragraphs: Make documents exporting a scenario as a JSON blueprint with modules, settings and mapped values. After import, create the account connections again; the file must be under 2 MB. Scenario history is exported separately as CSV, and Make warns that simple-mode AES keys are exposed in a shared scenario or downloaded blueprint. Inspect any export for secrets and test the required recovery scope before depending on it.

pros.text: Make's visual scenario workflow connects applications through triggers and actions that process data.
The credit documentation distinguishes fixed and dynamic consumption, giving users a unit they can inspect during a trial.
Make documents JSON blueprints for backing up, reusing and importing individual scenarios, with account connections recreated after import.

cons.text: Credit use may be dynamic: AI and advanced features can vary with tokens, file size, page count or processing time.
A displayed monthly credit quantity alone does not establish the cost of a scenario; module behavior and billing cadence must be checked.
Make warns that a simple-mode AES secret key is exposed when sharing a scenario or downloading its blueprint; review exported files before sharing them.

faqs.question: Does every Make action use exactly one credit?
faqs.answer: No. Most fixed-use app modules default to one credit per operation, while exceptions and dynamic AI or advanced features can consume a different amount.

faqs.question: What does Make Core cost for 10,000 monthly credits?
faqs.answer: The official pricing selector lists USD 12/month with monthly payment or USD 9/month equivalent on annual billing. Confirm location-dependent taxes and the final checkout total.

faqs.question: How should I estimate a scenario?
faqs.answer: Map its triggers, action modules, bundles and run frequency, then test retries and any AI, file or page processing against the current credit rules.

faqs.question: Can I back up or move a Make scenario?
faqs.answer: Make documents exporting a scenario as a JSON blueprint containing modules, settings and mapped values, and describes using blueprints to back up a scenario when switching Make accounts. Import requires creating your own account connections and the file must be under 2 MB. Scenario history has a separate CSV export. These sources do not establish full-organization recovery; no migration was tested.

faqs.question: Can I safely share every Make blueprint?
faqs.answer: Review the scenario before sharing. Make warns that a simple-mode AES secret key is exposed when a scenario is shared or its blueprint is downloaded. Do not distribute an export containing a secret; use approved secret handling and verify the selected module configuration.

verdict: Evaluate Make when a visual scenario builder and a broad app-connection workflow fit the use case. Forecast module actions and verify the current pricing selectors before estimating cost.
bestFor: Builders who prefer visual automation and can map expected module actions
notFor: Teams that need a verified self-hosted deployment or a fixed cost without a usage estimate
migration: Make documents JSON blueprints for individual scenarios: they include modules, module settings and mapped values, and can be used to back up scenarios when switching Make accounts. After import, create the account connections again; the imported file must be under 2 MB. Scenario history exports separately as CSV. Inspect exports for secrets because Make warns simple-mode AES keys are exposed when a scenario is shared or its blueprint is downloaded. Confirm the required organization-level recovery scope and rehearse a representative move; no migration was tested.
gaps: Confirm location-dependent checkout taxes and total; whether a customer-selectable region meets the intended account data-residency requirement; workspace-specific workflow and connected-provider data scope, configured log categories/periods, deletion response and purge timing; the applicable DPA/subprocessor list and legal suitability; and the exact organization resources that must be recoverable beyond an individual scenario blueprint.
A representative workflow has not been measured; credit use can vary by module and usage. No blueprint was imported, and exported scenarios were not inspected for actual secret values.
